This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there are some typographical errors in page-4 of the writ petition.
Let learned counsel for the petitioners file a typed copy of the said page correcting the typographical errors.
Mr. Amitav Das, learned counsel appearing for the N.H.A.I. submits that the State Government is to execute the work in question and N.H.A.I. has no role in it.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that earlier the petitioners approached this Court in W.P.(C) No.9292 of 2024 for a direction for compliance of the procedure in accordance with the provisions of law provided under the National Highways Act, 1956 and the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

1

The said writ petition was disposed of with a direction that the grievance of the petitioners shall be considered taking into account the instruction of the Government issued on 22.03.2022 under Annexure-11 as expeditiously as possible preferably within a period of six weeks from the date of communication of the order.

In this writ petition in paragraph-18, it is stated that in spite of such order, even though the order was communicated on 09.05.2024, but nothing has been done so far,
therefore, the petitioners have filed a contempt petition bearing CONTC No.6854 of 2024, which is subjudiced before this Court and now the Opposite Parties are taking all steps to dispossess the petitioners.
Let learned counsel for the State obtain instruction on the averments made in pargraph-18 of the writ petition and apprise this Court on the next date about the development, if any, made after the earlier order was passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No.9292 of 2024.
Put up this matter in the week commencing from 21st October 2024.

Judge  (Chittaranjan Dash)
